To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) We show that adversarial images are not only perturbations, but are in fact valid samples from the data distribution, and (2) We show that MCMC sampling can be used to remove adversarial perturbations from images.

we propose an adversarial defense approach that uses MCMC sampling to transform adversarial inputs into non-adversarial images, which are classified by the original classifier without being misclassified by the adversarial attack; we demonstrate the effectiveness of this method on the MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 datasets, using the FGSM, BIM, and PGD attacks.

(1) We demonstrate a new method for adversarial purification of input images that is capable of securing classifiers that are not trained to defend against adversarial attacks, and (2) We show that this approach, in addition to being a viable defense against adversarial attacks on classifiers, is a powerful tool for understanding the long-run behavior of EBMs, and can be used for the first time to study the long-run dynamics of deep EBMs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
defending naturally-trained classifiers, which we accomplish by purifying the original image using MCMC sampling with an EBM
the following questions: (a) Can a defense approach be designed that is distinct from adversarial training and can secure naturally-trained models against adversarial attacks?
the question of whether it is possible to defend a classifier that has been trained on a natural data distribution against adversarial attacks, without changing the classifier.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EBM-based adversarial defense is the first to secure naturally-trained classifiers, while adversarial training has been shown to be effective for securing adversarially-trained classifiers.
our method is the only successful post-training defense method to date, and it is the first to secure a naturally-trained classifier.

our approach is the first defense to secure naturally-trained classifiers, is the first to defend against a wide class of attacks including those which can be crafted after training, and is the first to use a long-run stochastic process as a defense.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are the first to show that a defense can be built using the long-run dynamics of an EBM to remove adversarial noise from an image.
we show that a defense method that is based on a long-term dynamic process can successfully defend against adversarial attacks on a variety of image classification tasks.
we show how the dynamics of EBMs can be leveraged for the first time to defend deep classifiers against adversarial attacks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
adversarial purification using MCMC sampling with EBMs is capable of securing a naturally-trained classifier against a variety of attacks.
a simple, naturally trained EBM can provide effective adversarial purification for a wide range of classifiers.
the dynamics of the EBM, which are learned from the natural data distribution and not the adversarial distribution, are able to effectively remove adversarial signals.
